signal: CAI Software merged with Print ePS into three divisions and acquired Mar-Kov

email.body1:
Eric, saw CAI Software fold Print ePS and Mar-Kov into three operating divisions.

That much consolidation usually means buying signals pile up faster than the team can act on them, and slow signal-to-action is where pipeline quietly leaks. Our AI SDR turns a signal into a researched, written, followed-up touch with zero rep time: 3-5x more meetings per rep, no new hires.

I built a personalized signal play for CAI off your hiring and tech-stack data, and accounts showing those signals tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Eric, quick follow-up for CAI Software.

Across three new divisions, data hygiene and follow-up speed get hard to measure, so the lift from outbound stays murky. The fix is making each signal trigger a touch automatically and tracking what it returns.

Want 15 minutes? I'll walk you through a teardown of your current outbound and three things I'd change. Our best practices alone usually lift response rates 50 to 70 percent.
email.body3:
Eric, last bit of proof for CAI Software.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how CAI's reply rate likely compares to other manufacturing-ERP teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Eric, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If tightening signal-to-action across the divisions isn't a priority right now, no problem at all. Integrating two acquisitions is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your revops motion? I'll tailor it to CAI either way.
